### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/spec`, touching **11** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **7** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/api-surface/ui.json`, `packages/spec/authorable-surface/ui.json`, `packages/spec/declaration-map/ui.json`, …), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**2** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/protocol/objectui/layout-dsl.mdx`  _(via PageComponentSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_
- `content/docs/ui/pages.mdx`  _(via data.environments (literal, a string literal in a comment on a changed line), /api/v1/cloud/home (route, a path literal in ElementApiDataSourceSchema; a path literal in a comment on a changed line; a path literal in elementApiReadUrlRefusal))_

⛔ **2** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v15.mdx`  _(via PageComponentSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-7.mdx`  _(via PageComponentSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **7** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/api-surface/ui.json`, `packages/spec/authorable-surface/ui.json`, `packages/spec/declaration-map/ui.json`, …) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **140** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 275ad4229a791f31ec90da4a14621cd54a0dad02` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `ee5c892708c759f1d656ca4b7fae01f7755c1c57` — the merge of head `b6c1d0790be0d3ad23e9da5f9e90ac39b7202d57` into base `275ad4229a791f31ec90da4a14621cd54a0dad02`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin ee5c892708c759f1d656ca4b7fae01f7755c1c57 && git checkout ee5c892708c759f1d656ca4b7fae01f7755c1c57
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 275ad4229a791f31ec90da4a14621cd54a0dad02 b6c1d0790be0d3ad23e9da5f9e90ac39b7202d57 && git checkout -B drift-repro 275ad4229a791f31ec90da4a14621cd54a0dad02 && git merge --no-ff b6c1d0790be0d3ad23e9da5f9e90ac39b7202d57

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 275ad4229a791f31ec90da4a14621cd54a0dad02
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 275ad4229a791f31ec90da4a14621cd54a0dad02` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `b6c1d0790be0d3ad23e9da5f9e90ac39b7202d57`
Local-runs: none

Inputs: card #23016 (body + 4 comments: triage 6122981517, claim 6125940052, os-dev-report 6129105136, seat ACCEPT 6129155601), PR #23079 (body, 17-file list, net diff `466380132..b6c1d0790`, +634/-31), the check-runs on the head, and the pinned objectui `7578323a544e` read as git objects. Nothing was built, run or re-run.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **`PageComponentSchema.dataSource` widens** from `ElementDataSourceSchema.optional()` to `z.union([ElementDataSourceSchema, ElementApiDataSourceSchema]).optional()`. The accept set grows by exactly the ruled shape `{ provider: 'api', read: { url, method? }, path? }`; the object arm's body has no hunk, and `authorable-surface/ui.json` and `json-schema.manifest/ui.json` change by additions only. **Right.** The plain union (not `discriminatedUnion`) is right too: zod 4's discriminated form needs the key on every option, and a `provider: 'object'` would be a second spelling of the object binding and a change to the def objectui imports by reference at the pin (`packages/types/src/zod/objectql.zod.ts` lines 622, 935, 2266: `stripImportedDefaults(SpecElementDataSourceSchema)`). The one visible cost, a refused object binding now arriving as `invalid_union` at `dataSource` with the old issue in the object branch, is disclosed in the changeset and re-pinned in `page.test.ts`. **Right.**

2. **Two new public exports**: `ElementApiDataSourceSchema` (const) and `ElementApiDataSource` (type, `z.input`), recorded in `api-surface/ui.json`, `declaration-map/ui.json`, `export-origins/ui.json`, `json-schema.manifest/ui.json`, and three `authorable-surface` rows `ui/ElementApiDataSource:{provider,read,path}`; isomorphic pin added (`type-alias-convention.pin.test.ts`, 775 to 776). **Right** - no `ElementApiDataSourceParsed` is owed: `method` is an optional literal with no `.default('GET')` (deliberately unlike `HttpRequestSchema`), and nothing in the tree transforms.

3. **`read.url` accept set** is the `.regex()` `^\/(?:[^/\\\x00-\x20\x7F][^\x00-\x20\x7F]*)?$`, so it projects as a JSON Schema `pattern` (a refinement would be dropped; `dropped-refinements.baseline.json` gains no site, two existing sites only moved path under `options[0]`). I re-derived all 23 refused and 3 admitted pin values by hand against the regex; every one agrees with the pins and with the published-pattern parity pin. The five named classes match objectui's `classifyNavigationTarget` at the pin (`packages/core/src/actions/navigationTarget.ts` lines 44-49: tab/LF/CR refused; `https?://`, `mailto:`; `./` admitted for a navigation; `/` admitted only when the second char is neither `/` nor a backslash): the API arm refuses the four cross-origin spellings that classifier refuses, and additionally `./`, on the measured `apiBase` promotion `/^\/(api|_auth|_account)\//` (`ActionRunner.ts` line 1987) - a `./` read would resolve against the SPA route, not the API. Refusal at `dataSource.read.url`, code `invalid_format`, class named, value never echoed. **Right.** Nit, not a defect: a mid-path space is refused as well (the browser would percent-encode it); the prescription says `%20`, and nothing previously accepted is narrowed since the arm is new.

4. **`read.method` admits `GET` alone** - narrower than the ruling's literal `method?`, and justified by measurement I confirmed at the pin: `ApiDataSource.find`, `findOne` and `aggregate` each pass `method: 'GET'` explicitly (`packages/core/src/adapters/ApiDataSource.ts` lines 246, 259, 362), overriding `options.method ?? base.method` (line 179). Declared equals enforced (PD #10). **Right.**

5. **`path`** is `^[A-Za-z0-9_-]+(?:\.[A-Za-z0-9_-]+)*$`, optional, refused at `dataSource.path` for JSONPath, brackets, slashes and empty segments - the ruling's "optional dotted path, e.g. `data.environments`". **Right.**

6. **Closed arm and closed read block** through `strictObject` with `aliases` and `guidance`. I read `packages/spec/src/shared/strict-object.ts`: `aliases` is consulted for the unknown-key REFUSAL message (ahead of the edit-distance fallback) and never admits the key, so `response/select/dataPath/responsePath -> path`, `fetch/request -> read`, `href/endpoint/path -> url`, `verb -> method` are prescriptions, not tolerated spellings - PD #12 holds and no ADR-0087 entry is owed. `headers`, `credentials`, `auth`, `authorization`, `token`, `apiKey` are refused at both levels with the signed-in-fetch prescription; `params` and `body` with their own fix; top-level `object`, `write`, `url`, `method` with guidance. "No credentials in metadata" is enforced at the door, not only described. **Right.**

7. **`[PLANNED - not yet rendered]` describe marker** instead of a ledger row. This is the ledger's own mechanism, not a workaround: `packages/spec/scripts/liveness/check-liveness.mts` lines 501-507 (`markerStatus`) grades a row-less property `planned` off `/\[planned/i`; the page walk stops at the undrilled `page/regions` container, so no component-level key can carry a row. `Spec property liveness` is green on the head. The `_note` sentence in `liveness/page.json` names the carrier (objectui#12197) in the same style the file already uses. **Right.** PD #10 corollary (nothing renders the binding yet, and the parse admits it on every component type): disclosed in the describe, the generated reference, the hand-written docs ("Not rendered yet") and the changeset, and the maintainer's ruling itself sequences objectui#12197 after this card. **Right, with disclosure.**

8. **Docs (acceptance 2)**: `content/docs/references/index.mdx` and `references/ui/page.mdx` are regenerated output (1523 to 1524 schemas; `PageComponent.dataSource[option 1]` / `[option 2]`), not hand edits; `content/docs/ui/pages.mdx` gains an "Element data sources" section with both shapes in one `os:check` fence (type-checked against the live spec in the lint lanes). `type: 'stat'` is a bare custom type outside the spec's reserved namespaces, so `component-type-unknown` (`packages/lint/src/validate-component-types.ts`) does not fire and the parse's open string arm admits it. **Right.**

9. **Remaining generated artifacts**: strictness-ledger counts (`ui/` 210 to 212 sites, `page.zod.ts` 9 to 11), `skills/objectstack-ui/references/_index.md` (`gen:skill-refs` headline line). `Type Check · source gates` and all six `Lint ·` lanes are green on the head. **Right.**

10. **Sibling checkout at objectui `7578323a544e`** (`.objectui-sha` on main; `Console Pin Gate` skips on `pull_request` by design, so I read it myself): the only typed read of the spec's `PageComponent` is `PageComponent['visibility']` (`packages/react/src/SchemaRenderer.tsx` line 191); `PageNodeSchema` omits `regions` from `SpecPage` (`PAGE_SPEC_EXCLUDED`, `layout.zod.ts` lines 1054-1060), so no typed `dataSource` flows in; block schemas import `ElementDataSourceSchema` by reference (unchanged); no objectui test pins `PageComponentSchema.shape.dataSource`. `useElementDataSource` admits a binding only through `isElementDataSourceConfig` (non-empty string `object`, `element-data-source.ts` lines 169-176), and `SchemaRenderer` strips `dataSource` from the props spread (line 2207), so an API binding reaches no block and shadows no adapter. The widening breaks nothing at the pin. **Right.**

11. **In-repo readers**: the diff touches no file in `@objectstack/lint`, `@objectstack/cli`, `metadata-protocol`, `sdui-parser`, `objectql` or the examples; the PR's reader audit (untyped `dataSource.object` reads fall through for a binding without `object`; both conversions touch only tombstoned flat keys or `dataSource.filter`) is consistent with the diff, and I did not re-read those sources. The verdicts for them are `Type Check · consumer gates` and `Test Core (1-6/6)`, in_progress at read time. **Right as far as the diff shows; CI convergence is the seat's read.**

### ② Semver level

`.changeset/23016-page-element-api-data-source.md`: `@objectstack/spec: minor`, body opening `Clause-②: yes (widening: a new accepted shape)`; the PR body carries the same line at line start. What the diff publishes: one new accepted shape, two new exports, no removal, no rename, no narrowing (the object arm is byte-identical; `GET`-only is a new key's admission, not a narrowing of anything previously accepted). `yes` takes at least `minor`; `(widening)` is the valid arm beside `yes`; nothing breaking, so no migration mapping and no ADR-0087 disposition marker is owed. `Check Changeset` is green on the head. The one TS-level consequence - `PageComponent['dataSource']` is now a union, so a typed `.object` read must narrow - has its single in-tree reader updated (`page.test.ts`) and no reader at the objectui pin (①.10). The changeset discloses the `invalid_union` envelope change and the not-rendered state in author-facing words. **`minor` is the right level; `Clause-②: yes (widening)` is the right declaration.**

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions`: `[]` - nothing to answer.
- Dev deviation, no liveness row: **answered** - the describe marker is the ledger's own `planned` mechanism (①.7); liveness gate green.
- Dev deviation, plain `z.union` with no `provider: 'object'`: **answered right** (①.1).
- Dev deviation, two files beyond the claim's list (`type-alias-convention.pin.test.ts`, `dropped-refinements.baseline.json`): **answered** - each gate-required; generated artifacts are the ones `check:generated` names.
- Dev deviation, `origin/main` merged via `os-regen-merge.sh`, main since moved: **answered** - the 17-file net diff against merge-base `466380132` is what this record judges; a later `main` is the queue's rebase.
- Dev flag, two cli unit contention timeouts rerun green: not a contract matter; `Test Core (1-6/6)` on the head are the verdicts, in_progress at read time.
- Out-of-scope 1, `check:platform-checklist` red at base `df7a137923`: the seat dropped it to the watchdog lane. **Agreed**, not this PR's.
- Out-of-scope 2, `@objectstack/lint` `page-walk` inherits the page's `object` for an API-bound node: **escalated to the seat.** The authoring door (`os validate` / `os lint`) is in THIS repository, and the first field-bearing API-bound block (objectui#12197) would have its field-shaped props judged against the page object. The dev's "carrier: none in this repository yet" leaves the lint half uncarried; recommend a lint-lane card here, sequenced with objectui#12197. Zero producers today, so not a blocker for this PR.
- Out-of-scope 3, objectui `apiBase` promotion hard-codes `/(api|_auth|_account)/` against a configurable REST `basePath`: objectui's; **carried** by objectui#12197.
- Out-of-scope 4, the view-level `ViewDataSchema` `api` arm (`HttpRequestSchema`) still admits a cross-origin `url`, `headers` and non-GET methods: the ruling scoped same-origin and no-credentials to the page-element binding, so this PR owes no carrier. **Escalated as a maintainer question** for the seat to put: does the view-level arm adopt the same rule?
- objectui follow-up for #12197: objectui's own describe prose at `objectql.zod.ts` line 335 and `public-blocks.zod.ts` lines 1069, 1255, 1448 says `PageComponentSchema.dataSource` declares `{ object, view?, filter?, sort?, limit? }` by reference; that prose goes stale at the next pin bump. **Escalated** as a note to carry on objectui#12197.
- Governed path, `skills/objectstack-ui/references/_index.md` (generator-owned `skills/**` row): the `Governed Surface Queue Guard` is green on this head, but its `pull_request` leg is an early warning that exits 0 (`scripts/pm/check-governed-queue-guard.mjs` header, line 40), so that green is NOT the lift. The lift is the `merge_group` leg's per-file recompute (the guard job now installs the toolchain) and, before the queue, the seat's own `--pr 23079` run on an installed tree. The seat already holds the PR as Tier H until that reading; this record lifts no Tier H path and is not that reading. **Open for the seat, outside the contract verdict.**
- Check-runs on the head at read time: green - Build Core, Build Docs, Check Changeset, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Lint & Repo Gates, six `Lint ·` lanes, Spec property liveness, Type Check · source gates, Type Check · debt ledger, Dogfood Regression Gate, Flag docs affected, Check Documentation Links, the claim / part-of / single-writer guards, Auto Label, Check PR Size. in_progress - Test Core (1/6 to 6/6), Type Check · workspace, Type Check · consumer gates. skipped by design - Console Pin Gate, Temporal Conformance, Dogfood shards, Packed-tarball smoke, Dogfood Verify CLI. No red. Landing waits on the in_progress lanes converging green; that is the seat's read, not this record's.
